Primary outcomes were inter- and intraindividual variability of cabotegravir and rilpivirine trough concentrations, expressed as percentage coefficient of variation (%CV).

concept.text: Inter- and intraindividual trough concentration variability

canonical_statement: Variability was classified as low when %CV was <20%, moderate at 20%–30%, and high when >30%.
Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) was used to assess intraindividual agreement; ICC <0.5 was poor, 0.5–0.75 moderate, and >0.75 good.
A secondary cabotegravir outcome was the proportion of trough concentrations below 4× the protein-adjusted IC90, defined as 664 ng/mL.

outcome.measurement_method: Plasma trough concentration by validated LC-MS/MS

canonical_statement: A secondary rilpivirine outcome was the proportion of trough concentrations below 4× the protein-adjusted IC90, defined as 48 ng/mL.

canonical_statement: Fisher exact and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests were used to assess factors associated with trough concentrations below 4×PA-IC90; analyses used SAS 9.4 with P<0.05 considered statistically significant.

canonical_statement: The clinical interpretation of trough concentrations is uncertain because multiple efficacy thresholds have been proposed, including 4×PA-IC90 and phase 3 first-trough-quartile upper limits (cabotegravir 1120 ng/mL; rilpivirine 32 ng/mL).
The authors stated that better-defined cabotegravir/rilpivirine exposure thresholds are needed to interpret pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationships for long-acting ART.
The study recruited participants from a single clinical site, limiting generalizability to more diverse populations; the cohort was predominantly male (80%).
Administration by four experienced nurses under controlled conditions may not reflect injection practices in other settings.
Only trough concentration variability was assessed; variability at other dosing-period time points and other pharmacokinetic parameters was not evaluated.
Only total plasma concentrations were assessed, which may not fully capture drug concentrations at the site of antiviral activity.
The study did not evaluate all potential covariates, including genetic polymorphisms and body-composition measures beyond BMI.
Persistent inter- and intraindividual variability in cabotegravir and rilpivirine trough concentrations remained after one year of continuous long-acting injectable use.
Because intraindividual variability persisted, the authors concluded that clinical TDM decisions should likely be based on more than one trough level.
The authors stated that long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine should not be discontinued solely because of a single low trough TDM level.
The study highlighted the need for continued research to refine pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic relationships for long-acting antiretroviral therapy.
